labels.mechanism: Disposal during dialog-content mount drains existing components, but mounting later siblings can still run effects. The retired branch clears dialog.Content before finally can unmount that completed subtree, orphaning those later effect cleanups.
labels.required_evidence: Describe disposal from a content setter followed by an effectful sibling, and why dropping rather than unmounting the completed subtree leaks cleanup.

labels.mechanism: Disposal from a replacement-content setter can retire the lifetime while UpdateContentDialog is in progress. Both content replacement paths resume and can reattach content to the disposed dialog, notably while native closing is deferred.
labels.required_evidence: Identify the live-update/replacement path and the need to check retirement after reentrant mount/update and clean abandoned replacements.

labels.mechanism: No fixture exercises ShowContentDialog's entry guard after disposal has started. A second sibling dialog can open after the first dialog setter disposes its host if that guard is removed.

findings.title: The Opened handler retains the owning host after dialog teardown
findings.evidence: The changed handler captures both reconciler and lifetime. Neither StopTracking (lines 79–83) nor ShowContentDialogCore's finally unsubscribes it. Consequently, retaining a closed dialog through .Set retains its reconciler and host: ReactorHostControl assigns itself to the reconciler's ThemeAnchor and Owner and installs host-capturing delegates (ReactorHostControl.cs:241–253). Clearing the dialog's content and tags does not break this new reference chain, so a disposed host removed from the window remains alive while the captured dialog is retained.
findings.recommendation: Store the Opened delegate and unsubscribe it in ShowContentDialogCore's finally, preserving the guard until a pending show completes. Add a lifetime regression fixture that retains the closed native dialog while verifying that its disposed, detached host can be collected.

adjudications.reason: Matches the pre-frozen retained-dialog leak. In c2, OverlayLifecycle.cs:334-341 captures reconciler/lifetime and its finally never detaches Opened. Reconciler.Owner is a strong property (Reconciler.cs:58), and host callbacks/theme anchor also retain the host. The dbcec359 repair changes this to a named handler detached in finally.

findings.title: RetireContentDialogs is unguarded and runs before any user cleanup, so one throwing Hide() can abort disposal
findings.evidence: RetireContentDialogs sets IsDisposingContentDialogs = true, then calls lifetime.Retire() in a plain foreach with no try/catch. Retire() calls dialog.Hide() and mutates the WinUI ContentDialog (Content, tags). Both hosts now call it first in Dispose(), and DisposeCollectingPropagation calls it before ForgetComponentDiagnostics and the cleanup loop. If any WinUI call throws (a COM error on a dialog in a bad state), the remaining lifetimes are not retired. The flag is already set, so a second call returns early and never retries. Effect cleanups, navigation teardown, and registry/theme unregistration are skipped. The patch's own comment says cleanup 'can throw', but this new step is the one placed ahead of the existing exception-collection machinery (issue #1291).
findings.recommendation: Wrap each Retire() in try/catch and feed failures into the existing pendingPropagation/RenderErrorHandler path, or at least guarantee the rest of Dispose still runs. Add a fixture where Hide() fails.

findings.title: Unsupported claim about native ShowAsync queueing, with an unverified timing-dependent mitigation
findings.evidence: The comment 'Hide before Opened need not cancel a queued native ShowAsync' asserts WinUI behavior, and the Opened handler re-calls Hide() on that basis. No in-repo source, test, or docs establish the claim. Retire() has already called Hide(), so this second Hide() runs only when that first call was ineffective. Only the PendingShow fixture touches this path, and it asserts end state after a fixed Render(100) delay.
findings.recommendation: Cite the in-repo evidence for the queued-ShowAsync behavior, or reword the comment as a defensive guard. Make the PendingShow fixture deterministic by waiting on the Closed/unloaded condition rather than sleeping.

findings.title: Multi-lifetime paths introduced by the new bookkeeping are not exercised
findings.evidence: ShowContentDialog now creates a new ContentDialogLifetime per rising edge and retires any prior pending one. s_liveDialogs.AddOrUpdate can overwrite an older, still-closing dialog's entry. Retire() then relies on ReferenceEquals(live.Lifetime, this) to avoid clearing the newer dialog's state. The eight new fixtures cover a single lifetime per anchor. None covers (a) re-open while the previous dialog is still closing, followed by host disposal, (b) a pending deferral replaced by a second rising edge, or (c) IsOpen toggled false while deferred, followed by disposal. There is also no non-UI unit test of the lifetime state machine, and none for the changed ShouldStartDeferredDialog gating.
findings.recommendation: Add a selftest that reopens during a Closing deferral and then disposes, asserting both dialogs are hidden and no OnClosed fires. Add one for a pending-then-replaced deferral, and a unit test of Retire/StopTracking set membership.

findings.title: Leftover debug output and stale 'baseline failure' rescue framing in a committed fixture
findings.evidence: The fixture prints a '# DialogDispose before rescue: ...' Console.WriteLine diagnostic, and the finally comment says 'the baseline failure cannot strand a modal dialog'. Both are scaffolding from reproducing the bug, not assertions. They add noisy selftest output and describe a pre-fix state that no longer exists.

However, the proposed COM-error/bad-state trigger is not demonstrated for a supported UI-thread disposal sequence. ContentDialogThemeBinding.Dispose only detaches a handler (lines 76-81). Not T1: the finding asks for reopen/multiple-lifetime scenarios, not a second dialog entering after host disposal. findings.title: Retained native dialogs now retain their owning hosts
findings.evidence: The new Opened delegate captures both reconciler and lifetime. StopTracking only removes the lifetime from its owner's set (line 83), and the completion finally (lines 374–395) never unsubscribes this delegate. A native dialog retained through .Set therefore retains its reconciler after closing or disposal. ReactorHostControl assigns itself to that reconciler's Owner and RenderErrorHandlerProvider (ReactorHostControl.cs:249–253), so the disposed host remains reachable even after Content and element tags are cleared.
findings.recommendation: Keep a removable Opened handler and unsubscribe it in ShowContentDialogCore's terminal finally, retaining the queued-open protection until ShowAsync finishes. Add a selftest retaining the closed native dialog while checking that its disposed host can be collected.

findings.title: Canceled pre-show mounts can strand effects created after disposal
findings.evidence: Consider a dialog body whose first child's OnMount calls host.Dispose(), followed by an effectful component sibling. Disposal clears _componentNodes (Reconciler.cs:7965), but panel mounting continues through subsequent children (V1HandlerAdapter.cs:273–282). The later component is registered and its effects run (Reconciler.Mount.cs:902–923). This new retired branch then clears Content and returns, so the finally's content-dependent UnmountChild never cleans that sibling. Subsequent host.Dispose() calls short-circuit. The BeforeShow fixture only disposes from the dialog setter after mounting a plain TextBlock, so it misses this resource leak.
findings.recommendation: Abort further dialog-body mounting after retirement, or roll back nodes and effects created after the disposal sweep before discarding the body. Extend BeforeShow with disposal from an early child's OnMount and a later effectful sibling, asserting no surviving subscription.

adjudications.reason: Matches the pre-frozen retained-dialog leak, with the missing unsubscription and host-retention chain established in the c2 source and repaired by dbcec359.

Matches the pre-frozen residual-subtree effect leak. The proposed OnMount trigger is equivalent to the original setter trigger: Reconciler.cs:6358-6360 invokes OnMountAction synchronously during each child's mount. Later siblings can therefore mount after disposal clears the component set. OverlayLifecycle.cs:367-371 then drops Content before finally can unmount that subtree. findings.title: Native-identity guidance inserted under the wrong heading, splitting the mutation-check section
findings.evidence: The new paragraph sits directly under `### Mutation checks must prove the mutation ran` (line 139). The section's original first paragraph, `Before interpreting a green mutation run...`, now follows it. The new text is about selftest control identity (ReactorState vs RuntimeHelpers.GetHashCode), not about checking that a mutation ran. A reader of the mutation-testing section first gets unrelated identity advice, and the identity rule has no heading of its own, so it is hard to find from the 'When to write which test' material.
findings.recommendation: Move the paragraph to its own subsection, for example `### Native control identity in selftests`, placed before `### Mutation checks must prove the mutation ran`, and leave the mutation section starting with its original paragraph.

findings.title: New per-anchor ConditionalWeakTable instead of the attached-state store
findings.evidence: `s_pendingDialogs = new ConditionalWeakTable<FrameworkElement, ContentDialogLifetime>()` adds a second weak table keyed by the managed wrapper of the placeholder anchor. The same diff's CHANGELOG (spec 047 §3 entry) and its TESTING.md note both say managed wrappers can be collected while the native control survives, which is why per-element state was moved to native attached state. Today the entry works only because `ContentDialogLifetime` strongly captures `anchor` and the reconciler's `ContentDialogLifetimes` set roots that lifetime. If the set membership changes, the lookups in `TryTakeLiveContentDialog`/`ShowContentDialog` would silently miss.
findings.recommendation: Keep the pending lifetime in the anchor's `ReactorAttached.StateProperty` / ReactorState, or add a comment saying the strong anchor reference in `ContentDialogLifetime` is load-bearing for this CWT.

findings.title: Dialog retirement runs before the guarded cleanup scope, so a throw aborts all disposal after `_disposed = true`
findings.evidence: `_reconciler.RetireContentDialogs()` runs right after `_disposed = true` and outside `RenderErrorDispatch.EnterPropagationScope()`. `Retire()` calls `Theme?.Dispose()`, `dialog.Content = null` and `dialog.Hide()` on native objects. If any of these throws (for example, a dialog whose XamlRoot or window is already torn down), `ThemeResourceListeners.Unregister`, every effect cleanup, and `DisposeCollectingPropagation` are skipped. A second Dispose is then a no-op. `IsDisposingContentDialogs` is already true, so the remaining lifetimes are never retired either. ReactorHost.cs line 1562 has the same issue. Before this change, nothing could throw at that point.
findings.recommendation: Make retirement best-effort: wrap each `lifetime.Retire()` in try/catch and feed failures into the same pending-propagation and RenderErrorHandler path as other cleanup failures, so the rest of disposal always runs.

adjudications.reason: The paragraph is indeed under the mutation-check heading, but moving it is an editorial organization preference. No incorrect instruction or substantive behavioral consequence is demonstrated, so it is excluded by the frozen high-signal review contract, consistently with P2 finding 4.

The finding overlooks an explicit local exception. OverlayLifecycle.cs:44-53 explains why rare feature-local native associations use side tables rather than adding slots to every ReactorState. The lifetime strongly captures the anchor and is rooted by ContentDialogLifetimes (lines 61-64 and 211-212); the finding itself concedes the current invariant holds. A hypothetical future membership change is not a defect in this snapshot. This exposes tension between the broad rubric rule and documented local prior art.

Same unresolved native-exception hypothesis as P2 finding 0. The early-call position and idempotency flags are real, but no supported sequence that makes the cited native operations throw has been demonstrated. The conditional hypothesis is not credited as a confirmed runtime defect, and agreement between two reports does not establish it.
